items.prompt: Four measurements of a diameter are 2.46 mm, 2.52 mm, 2.48 mm and 2.50 mm. Estimate the percentage uncertainty in the mean diameter.
items.canonical_answer: Range = 2.52 − 2.46 = 0.06 mm, so the absolute uncertainty is 0.03 mm. The mean is 2.49 mm. Percentage uncertainty = 0.03 ÷ 2.49 = 0.012, which is 1.2%.
marking_guidance: Working: half the range as the absolute uncertainty, then divided by the mean - the step that earns the mark.
Final answer: about 1.2%, as a percentage with no unit of length. The full range (2.4%) is the common slip.

items.prompt: A straight line of best fit on a graph of T² / s² (y-axis) against L / m (x-axis) passes through (0.250, 1.02) and (0.650, 2.62). Determine the gradient of the line, with its unit.
items.canonical_answer: Gradient = Δy/Δx = (2.62 − 1.02) / (0.650 − 0.250). Δy = 1.60 s² and Δx = 0.400 m, and 1.60 ÷ 0.400 = 4.00, so the gradient is 4.00 s² m⁻¹. The two points are far apart on the line, which keeps the reading error small.
marking_guidance: Reading: two points on the line, far apart - 1 mark; the gradient value 4.00 - 1 mark.
The unit means s² per metre, the unit of y over the unit of x: s² m⁻¹.

items.prompt: On a graph whose x-axis starts at 0.200 m, the line of best fit has gradient 4.00 s² m⁻¹ and passes through (0.250, 1.02). Determine the y-intercept.
items.canonical_answer: The x-axis does not start at zero, so the intercept is calculated, not read: c = y − mx. 4.00 × 0.250 = 1.00, and 1.02 − 1.00 = 0.02, so c = 0.02 s².
marking_guidance: Reading: c = y − mx with a point on the line; reading the value where the line meets the left-hand edge of the grid gives the wrong intercept - the mark depends on this.

items.prompt: A learner says that taking ten repeat readings removes the zero error on a newton-meter. Explain the error.
items.canonical_answer: Repeating and averaging reduces only random error, because the scatter partly cancels. A zero error is a systematic error: it shifts every reading by the same amount, so the mean of any number of readings carries it too. It is removed by zeroing the meter or subtracting the offset.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: the confusion named - repeats reduce random error, not a systematic error such as a zero error.

items.prompt:
A pendulum of length L swings with period T. These are our readings for six lengths, each T found from timing 20 swings twice:

| L / m | T / s | T² / s² |
|---|---|---|
| 0.200 | 0.90 | 0.81 |
| 0.300 | 1.10 | 1.21 |
| 0.400 | 1.27 | 1.61 |
| 0.500 | 1.42 | 2.02 |
| 0.600 | 1.55 | 2.40 |
| 0.700 | 1.68 | 2.82 |

It is suggested that T² = kL + c, where k and c are constants.
(a) Explain why 20 swings were timed and not one. [1]
(b) Justify the number of significant figures in the T² column. [1]
(c) Plot a graph of T² / s² on the y-axis against L / m on the x-axis on your own graph paper, choosing scales so the points cover at least half the grid, and draw the line of best fit. [3]
(d) Determine the gradient and the y-intercept of your line. [2]
(e) Hence state the values of k and c, with their units. [1]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) The uncertainty in starting and stopping the watch is shared over 20 swings, so the percentage uncertainty in T is 20 times smaller.
(b) T is recorded to 2 or 3 significant figures, so T² is given to 3, matching the raw data with the most significant figures in the calculation.
(c) With L from 0.200 m to 0.700 m and T² from 0.81 s² to 2.82 s², a scale of 0.1 m per 2 cm on the x-axis (a false origin at 0.200 m) and 0.2 s² per 2 cm on the y-axis fills more than half the grid. The six points lie close to one straight line.
(d) Using the points (0.250, 1.01) and (0.650, 2.61) on the line: Δy = 1.60 s² and Δx = 0.400 m, and 1.60 ÷ 0.400 = 4.00, so the gradient is 4.00 s² m⁻¹. The x-axis starts at 0.200 m, so the intercept is calculated: 4.00 × 0.250 = 1.00, and 1.01 − 1.00 = 0.01 s².
(e) k = 4.00 s² m⁻¹ and c = 0.01 s², close to zero.
marking_guidance: Table and column headings: the T² column carries quantity / unit (T² / s²) - part (b).
Graph: the scales, the plotted points and the line - 3 marks in (c); the gradient from a large triangle on the line and the intercept by calculation - 2 marks in (d).
Conclusion: k and c with their units in (e) - 1 mark; a value with no unit is not a value.
